\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹھوکر} (ṭhokar)}{ٹھوکر (ṭhokar)}]{\ur{ٹھوکر} (ṭhokar) — a stumble; a knock of the foot}

\label{lesson:UR-C285-thokar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to overturn, then the Urdu for a ride.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹھوکر}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھوکر}} — \emph{ṭhokar} — \textquotedblleft{}a stumble; a knock of the foot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مجھے} \ur{پتھر} \ur{سے} \ur{ٹھوکر} \ur{لگی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mujhe patthar se ṭhokar lagī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I tripped over a stone.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھوکر}} (\emph{ṭhokar}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭhokar}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ṭhōkk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5513). The one who trips takes \textbf{\ur{مجھے}}: \textbf{\ur{مجھے} \ur{ٹھوکر} \ur{لگی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhokar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhokar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujhe patthar se ṭhokar lagī.} — I tripped over a stone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to overturn, then the Urdu for a ride, then say \emph{ṭhokar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ٹھوکر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A stumble; a knock of the foot\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لڑکھڑانا} (laṛkhaṛānā)}{لڑکھڑانا (laṛkhaṛānā)}]{\ur{لڑکھڑانا} (laṛkhaṛānā) — to stagger}

\label{lesson:UR-C285-larkharana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a ride, then the Urdu for a stumble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لڑکھڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لڑکھڑانا}} — \emph{laṛkhaṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to stagger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{لڑکھڑا} \ur{کر} \ur{گر} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh laṛkhaṛā kar gir gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He staggered and fell.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لڑکھڑایا}, \emph{voh laṛkhaṛāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لڑکھڑانا}} (\emph{laṛkhaṛānā}) is set by CDIAL under Sanskrit \emph{laṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}shakes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10916), where the Hindi cousin appears as \emph{larkharānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to stumble\textquotedblright{}. The repeated \emph{-khaṛ-} gives the unsteady steps.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkhaṛānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh laṛkhaṛā kar gir gayā.} — He staggered and fell.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a ride, then the Urdu for a stumble, then say \emph{laṛkhaṛānā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پاؤں} (pāoṅ)}{پاؤں (pāoṅ)}]{\ur{پاؤں} (pāoṅ) — a foot}

\label{lesson:UR-C285-paon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a stumble, then the Urdu for to stagger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پاؤں}}
\textbf{\ur{پاؤں}} — \emph{pāoṅ} — \textquotedblleft{}a foot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{پاؤں} \ur{پھسل} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā pāoṅ phisal gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My foot slipped.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پاؤں}} (\emph{pāoṅ}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{pāda}, \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8056), where CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pā̃u}. Urdu writes it with \textbf{\ur{ؤ}} and the nasal \textbf{\ur{ں}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چھلنا} (chhilnā)}{چھلنا (chhilnā)}]{\ur{چھلنا} (chhilnā) — to be grazed; to be scraped}

\label{lesson:UR-C285-chhilna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to stagger, then the Urdu for a foot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چھلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{چھلنا}} — \emph{chhilnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be grazed; to be scraped\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{گھٹنا} \ur{چھل} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā ghuṭnā chhil gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I grazed my knee.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{گھٹنا} \ur{چھل} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh ghuṭnā chhil gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
belongs with \emph{chīlnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to peel\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under \emph{*chilla}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5051); \textbf{\ur{چھلنا}} is the skin coming off by itself, in a fall.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to stagger, then the Urdu for a foot, then say \emph{chhilnā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خراش} (kharāsh)}{خراش (kharāsh)}]{\ur{خراش} (kharāsh) — a scratch; a graze}

\label{lesson:UR-C285-kharash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a foot, then the Urdu for to be grazed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خراش}}
\textbf{\ur{خراش}} — \emph{kharāsh} — \textquotedblleft{}a scratch; a graze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہاتھ} \ur{پر} \ur{ایک} \ur{خراش} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hāth par ek kharāsh thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a scratch on the hand.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خراش}} (\emph{kharāsh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kharāsh}, \textquotedblleft{}a scratching, a scraping\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{ایک} \ur{خراش} \ur{تھی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
